findings.title: Purged nested diagrams leave installation active
findings.why_it_matters: For an existing installation whose recorded diagrams directory is the app directory or a descendant, an explicitly confirmed purge still sets preserve_app_for_diagrams=1. The uninstall then skips removing the app and ownership state; even when safe_purge_diagrams deletes the app itself, the ownership marker remains, so a command reported as uninstall leaves the installation recorded and future update/doctor behavior treats it as installer-owned.
findings.suggested_fix: Only preserve the app for nested diagrams when PURGE_DIAGRAMS is empty; for a confirmed purge, remove the app and state as part of the normal uninstall path (and tolerate the subsequent purge target already being absent).
evidence: Lines 601-605 set preserve_app_for_diagrams whenever diagrams_within_app succeeds, without considering whether the user explicitly requested a purge.
Lines 647-655 skip both app and state removal whenever preserve_app_for_diagrams is 1, while lines 660-664 purge only the diagram target afterward.
A recorded DIAGRAMS_DIR equal to APP_DIR causes safe_purge_diagrams to delete APP_DIR but leaves STATE_FILE intact because the state-removal branch was skipped.

findings.title: Failed skill staging leaves hidden directories
findings.why_it_matters: If copying the packaged skill or writing its marker fails after mktemp succeeds, set -e exits into rollback but the client-local staging directory is outside TEMP_DIR and is not removed. Failed installs therefore are not fully transactional and can accumulate hidden, installer-created skill copies under the client configuration directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the current staged skill path and remove it from cleanup when it still exists, clearing the variable after the directory is moved into place.
evidence: Line 466 creates staged_skill under destination_parent rather than under TEMP_DIR.
Lines 468-473 can terminate under set -e before staged_skill is moved to destination.
Cleanup at lines 89-91 removes only TEMP_DIR, and rollback_install restores registered destination snapshots but has no record of staged_skill.

findings.title: WSL smoke assumes C:\Temp already exists
findings.why_it_matters: C:\Temp is not a standard directory guaranteed to exist on Windows. On a normal WSL2 machine without /mnt/c/Temp, mktemp fails before the mounted-Windows executable shims are created, so the documented release smoke never tests the intended WSL rejection path.
findings.suggested_fix: Create and validate the mounted-Windows parent first, or have the operator select an existing writable directory under /mnt/<drive> before running mktemp.
evidence: Line 24 calls mktemp with /mnt/c/Temp as the parent.
The preceding commands create only directories below smoke_root; no step creates or verifies /mnt/c/Temp.

residual_risks: Registration discovery treats any nonzero `mcp get` result as `missing`; whether a transient client/config error could make `mcp add` overwrite an existing registration depends on each external CLI's duplicate-name behavior.
Rollback restores whole client config files, so concurrent client config writes during installation would be lost; the reviewed code has no locking or merge mechanism.
testing_gaps: The rollback scenario starts with no existing installer-owned app or state, so it does not verify that a failed update restores the previous app tree, ownership marker, package version, and client skills.
No fault-injection test fails during skill copying/marker creation, so client-local staging-directory cleanup is unverified.
The nested-diagrams uninstall branch is not tested for either preservation without purge or complete removal with an explicitly confirmed purge.
